newsitem.title: INDIA: Shoe haul found at Indian ex-movie star's homes.
newsitem.headline: Shoe haul found at Indian ex-movie star's homes.

text.p: Indian police have seized 10,500 sarees and 750 pairs of shoes from the country's best-known woman politician who has been arrested on corruption charges, domestic news agencies reported on Friday.

Police also seized nearly a tonne of silver and 28 kg (61.6 lb) of gold in raids last weekend at homes owned by Jayalalitha Jayaram, a former movie star and former chief minister of the southern state of Tamil Nadu, the United News of India news agency said.

The shoe collection evokes memories of former Philippine First Lady Imelda Marcos, who had 3,000 pairs of designer shoes and was accused along with her husband Ferdinand of looting the national treasure of $5 billion while he was president.
Jayalalitha was arrested in a corruption case last Saturday, seven months after she was routed in regional elections. Following the arrest, police searched her two homes.

The 48-year-old politician, whose regional party was an electoral ally of former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao's Congress party, has denied any wrongdoing and accused the state government that replaced hers of a vendetta.

"During the search, the following moveable properties were found -- 10,500 sarees, of which 750 were of pure silk, worth about nine million rupees," UNI said, quoting a list submitted by investigators to a judge hearing the case.
It also listed "750 pairs of new footwear with colours matching the sarees, worth about 225,000 rupees."
The gold and silver seized from Jayalalitha's sprawling residence in Madras was initially estimated to be worth about $16.5 million.
"The seizures included 91 watches, 44 air conditioners, 19 cars and documents relating to the purchase of properties to the tune of 250 million rupees," the agency said.
In the case in which she was arrested, police accuse her of excess spending totalling 85 million rupees on 45,302 television sets for villagers while she was chief minister.
Jayalalitha has been charged in seven corruption cases including violations of foreign exchange and income tax laws.
The seized gold included 700 gold bangles, several diamond ear studs, necklaces, bracelets, waist belts and gold dinner plates, police were quoted as saying.
Jayalalitha's home, set on 15 acres, had expensive Italian marble and granite fittings, as well as a small movie theatre, the report said.
